newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed lower on Friday, drifting for much of the session as investors monitored continuing mark and guilder weakness against the dollar.

Dealers said trading volumes were heavier than usual for a Friday, especially at the longer end, with some detecting signs of switching from 30 year paper where the 7.5 percent 2023 bond closed off 0.30 at 116.45/65.
"We're quite bearish again, much of it is definitely currency driven but there's also a bit of profit-taking at the longer end," one dealer said.
"A lot of what we've seen today has just been a bit of a shake out from a rally late yesterday. There's also been some pressure on the bunds, and guilders are following Germany," said another dealer.
Dealers said some investors appeared to be steering money into the shorter end where declines were held to a minimum. The 7.50 percent June 1999 bond closed down 0.03 at 106.39/49.

"A lot of clients are holding back and contemplating what to do with the recent flattening in the yield curve. They're asking themselves whether they should take some profit in the longer end and increase exposure in the short end," said a dealer.

Some said they had anticipated bonds would recover a little towards the end of the day, although in the longer term recent currency weakness could point to a tightening in interest rates. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
